common_name: Black Tower Elderberry (Columnar Dark-Purple-Leaved Ornamental Elder)

planting.note: Its narrow, upright habit makes it a good pick where a dark-foliaged elderberry is wanted but garden width is limited.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, evenly moist soil and give afternoon shade in hot climates to keep the near-black foliage from scorching. Prune out about a third of the oldest canes each late winter to keep the columnar form dense and encourage new flowering wood. Pair with a genetically distinct elderberry cultivar nearby to improve pollination and berry set, since the dark leaf color is the main draw but the pink-white flower clusters still ripen into small edible (cooked-only) black fruit. Expect a slower, more restrained growth habit than green-leaved elderberry types.

common_name: Instant Karma Elderberry (Compact Golden-Leaved Pink-Flowered Elder)

planting.note: Give it partial shade in warm climates, since golden foliage is prone to leaf scorch in full Gulf Coast summer sun.

directions: Site this compact selection where its chartreuse-to-gold foliage and deep pink flower clusters can be seen up close, ideally with some midday shade to prevent bleaching in hot summers. Water regularly during the first two seasons to establish a full root system, then reduce to moderate irrigation once mature. Plant a second, genetically distinct elderberry cultivar within pollination range to improve fruit set, since the small dark berries that follow the flowers are cooked-only edible and secondary to this cultivar's ornamental role. Cut back hard in late winter if a smaller, denser shrub is preferred, as it flowers on new wood.
